sourceFacts.fact: A white or absent expected red reflex may reflect serious ocular disease, including retinoblastoma or cataract.
Leukocoria needs prompt ophthalmologist assessment; its appearance alone does not identify the cause.

expectedLabels: Abnormal red reflex: a signal to act
layoutSpecification: Title 'Abnormal red reflex: a signal to act'. LEFT three small abstract indicator tiles stacked vertically, no eye shapes: top tile a white circle with navy outline labelled 'White'; middle tile an empty dark-grey circle labelled 'Absent'; bottom tile TWO circles of unequal warm-red brightness labelled 'Unequal'. Do not use clinical photograph lighting, pupil or iris texture. Three clear arrows merge into one large arrow at centre pointing RIGHT to an urgent appointment card labelled 'Urgent ophthalmology'. To its right a magnifying glass over a plain question-mark token, labelled 'Find the cause'; beneath 'Including retinoblastoma'. Very small bottom 'Symbols only • not diagnostic images'. Diagram must not imply every warning sign equals retinoblastoma; it leads to evaluation of possible causes.
